consequences: Artifact commands and storage contracts are exposed via Protocol, Core, and SDK, and agent contracts and context packets now default to canonical artifact operations.
All unit, integration, and quality gates pass.

decisions.statement: First-party agent surfaces (agent-cli, providers, launcher delegation, credentials command) are audited and scheduled for staged retirement in docs/planning/0.26/FIRST_PARTY_AGENT_AUDIT_AND_RETIREMENT_PLAN.md.
decisions.reasoning: AutoForge/Priozar is a deterministic engineering control plane. Interactive conversational agent runtime and model custody belong to CoJack Labs AI, while vendor-neutral contracts and structured handoffs remain in the framework.
consequences: Retain third-party agent contracts, handoffs, and orchestration; deprecate bare command delegation and credentials commands; prepare removal of apps/agent-cli and packages/providers.

decisions.statement: Framework identity and compatibility constants are centralized in @cojacklabs/autoforge-protocol under packages/protocol/src/compatibility.ts, establishing Priozar as the successor bundle and AutoForge as the compatibility bundle while superseding the rejected Forger proposal.
decisions.reasoning: A single source of truth for product, executable, package, state-directory, and environment identifiers prevents fragmented migration logic across Core, Protocol, SDK, CLI, and state managers.
consequences: FRAMEWORK_IDENTITY, frameworkExecutableSchema, and stateDirectorySchema are exported from Protocol and re-exported from Core vocabularies, with automated schema tests enforcing supported boundaries.

decisions.statement: Implemented recoverable AutoForge-to-Priozar brand migration in src/migrations/brand.ts and wired into autoforge migrate brand, supporting dry-run inspection, dual-directory conflict detection, mutation locking, recoverable backup, atomic staging and publication, and contract updates.
decisions.reasoning: Framework migration from .autoforge to .priozar must be deterministic, non-destructive, reversible via backups, and guarded against dual-state conflict without touching user source files.
consequences: autoforge migrate brand [--dry-run] [--json] is exposed in CLI help and reference docs, tested with automated conflict, dry-run, and atomic apply suites.

decisions.statement: Added bin/priozar.js and registered the priozar binary in package.json under the @cojacklabs/autoforge package, establishing a dual-executable bridge for the Priozar successor line.
decisions.reasoning: Users and agents can invoke the CLI as either autoforge or priozar during the compatibility window, allowing seamless script transition before standalone @cojacklabs/priozar publication.
consequences: bin/priozar.js and bin/autoforge.js both route through dist/cli.js, verified with npm pack --dry-run and manual binary execution.

decisions.statement: Completed Priozar brand migration documentation and release guidance, authoring docs/PRIOZAR_BRAND_MIGRATION_GUIDE.md and updating README.md and docs/README.md with dry-run, apply, rollback, and dual-executable usage.
decisions.reasoning: Clear documentation for the Priozar transition ensures users and external agents understand the transition window, dual executable availability, non-destructive migration commands, and recovery procedures.
consequences: docs/PRIOZAR_BRAND_MIGRATION_GUIDE.md is published, linked from docs/README.md and README.md, covering safety invariants, conflict handling, and post-migration verification.

decisions.statement: Rename AutoForge to Priozar with a compatibility window and untouched history
decisions.reasoning: The existing migration guide already defines Priozar as the successor identity with a bridge. A hard cut would break installed CLIs and 18 registered projects, and rewriting historical documents would falsify what things were called at the time.
consequences: priozar becomes the primary name for code, packages, binaries, state and live docs, while autoforge aliases and the .autoforge fallback remain for one to two releases.
dev/, older docs/planning versions, CHANGELOG entries and past decisions keep the AutoForge name.
npm publication, GitHub repository rename and domain changes are prepared here but performed by a human.

decisions.statement: Resolve the framework state directory through one shared resolver that prefers .priozar and falls back to .autoforge
decisions.reasoning: The state directory name was hardcoded in about 30 places. A single synchronous resolver in src/core/state-directory.ts lets the dual-read compatibility window be implemented and tested once, and means a project that has only .autoforge keeps working unchanged.
consequences: resolveStateDirectoryName/Path return .priozar when it exists and .autoforge otherwise, including when neither exists, so new state still lands where the installed CLI reads it.
Project discovery treats either directory as a project marker and keeps the marker value autoforge for compatibility.
Remaining hardcoded .autoforge call sites are tracked by task.adopt-the-state-directory-resolver-in-remaining-stores and must be converted before migrate brand can be applied.

decisions.statement: Map a leading .autoforge path segment to the active state directory inside resolveProjectPath
decisions.reasoning: Around 17 modules express state locations as .autoforge/... relative constants that all flow through resolveProjectPath. Rewriting at that single chokepoint makes them follow a migrated project without editing each constant or changing exported constant values.
consequences: resolveProjectPath and resolveContainedProjectPath rewrite only a whole leading .autoforge segment to .priozar when .priozar is active; .autoforge-notes and nested src/.autoforge paths are untouched.
Guardrail artifact-destination checks accept both state directories and quality scope excludes both evidence.json paths.
Sites that join the state directory name directly rather than going through resolveProjectPath still need per-site conversion, tracked by task.adopt-the-state-directory-resolver-in-remaining-stores.

decisions.statement: Convert direct state-directory joins to the shared resolver and leave legacy init creation unchanged for now
decisions.reasoning: Stores that go through resolveProjectPath were already covered by the central mapping, so only the sites that join the directory name themselves needed conversion. Verified end to end: the built CLI runs doctor, recap and status on a project containing only .priozar.
consequences: bootstrap, domain, governance, knowledge, orchestration, workflows, the agent contract store, inspectInstallation, worktree home and the agent-cli handoff directory now follow the active state directory.
autoforge init and the legacy migration still create .autoforge; choosing the directory for new projects is deferred to the packages and binaries phase.
agent-cli carries a small local copy of the resolver because it cannot import from the CLI src tree.

decisions.statement: Treat .autoforge/config.json as the project config and defer the root autoforge.config.json rename to the scripts task
decisions.reasoning: The v0.25 CLI reads its configuration from the state directory, which dual-read already resolves. The root autoforge.config.json is consumed only by legacy scripts and the v0.24 migration, so it has no CLI code path to make dual-read.
consequences: doctor now reports which state directory is active, and tests prove agent and specification initialization recognise .priozar/config.json as well as .autoforge/config.json.
Renaming the root file with a fallback in the legacy scripts is tracked by a new task in the live docs, CI and URLs phase.

decisions.statement: Brand migration copies, verifies and validates before removing .autoforge, and mirrors gitignore rules
decisions.reasoning: The first version moved the directory, reported validation without running it, listed a hardcoded dry-run plan, and wrote a framework field the contract schema does not allow. Copying first and removing the source last means any failure leaves the original intact, and mirroring the ignore rules keeps runtime state out of git under the new name.
consequences: migrate brand refuses a source installation that is not current, verifies the copy file by file, validates with the real installation check, and rolls back the new directory and gitignore on any failure.
The dry-run lists the real top-level entries and whether .gitignore will change, and the source is removed only after validation with a backup retained.
The agent contract is copied unchanged; its autoforge command text is updated when contracts are regenerated in the repository migration phase.

decisions.statement: Rename public protocol and SDK identifiers to Priozar with deprecated aliases; rename CLI-internal identifiers outright
decisions.reasoning: protocol and sdk are published library APIs, so consumers need the old names to keep working through the compatibility window. The CLI package ships only a bundle, so its internal names can change directly. String values that are wire or storage formats must not change.
consequences: PriozarError, PriozarErrorCode, PriozarErrorOptions, toPriozarError, priozarErrorCodeSchema, PRIOZAR_PROTOCOL_VERSION, PRIOZAR_AGENT_LAUNCH_PROTOCOL_VERSION, PRIOZAR_AGENT_RECURSION_ENV, PriozarSdk, PriozarSdkOptions, createPriozarSdk and SupportedPriozarOperations are canonical; the AutoForge-named equivalents remain as deprecated aliases.

Error name is now PriozarError. The credential service string com.cojacklabs.autoforge-agent and the AUTOFORGE_AGENT_LAUNCHED value are unchanged here because changing them would orphan stored credentials or break launched agents.
test/quality-gate.test.ts was left on the deprecated alias because editing it trips the secret scanner on its intentional dummy fixture; tracked as an issue.

decisions.statement: Resolve framework environment variables through one protocol helper that prefers PRIOZAR_ over AUTOFORGE_
decisions.reasoning: Four AUTOFORGE_ variables are read in different packages. A single readFrameworkEnv helper in the protocol package, built on the existing FRAMEWORK_IDENTITY env prefixes, keeps precedence identical everywhere and is shared by the CLI and the apps.
consequences: readFrameworkEnv(name, env) returns PRIOZAR_<name> when set, including an explicit empty string, else AUTOFORGE_<name>; frameworkEnvNames(name) names both.
PRIOZAR_HOME now overrides AUTOFORGE_HOME for the worktree directory; AUTOFORGE_HOME still works.
The launcher and agent-cli variables are handled by a sibling task because they live under apps, which this task's scope excludes.

decisions.statement: Switch the agent recursion guard to PRIOZAR_AGENT_LAUNCHED while still setting and honouring AUTOFORGE_AGENT_LAUNCHED
decisions.reasoning: The launcher marks the child process so a launched agent cannot launch another. A launcher and agent from different releases may be mixed during the compatibility window, so each side must recognise the other's marker or recursion protection silently fails.
consequences: PRIOZAR_AGENT_RECURSION_ENV is now PRIOZAR_AGENT_LAUNCHED and the deprecated AUTOFORGE_AGENT_RECURSION_ENV keeps its legacy value.
Recursion is detected from either marker, and launched children receive both.
PRIOZAR_NO_AGENT overrides AUTOFORGE_NO_AGENT, and the agent-cli reads PRIOZAR_OPENAI_MODEL before AUTOFORGE_OPENAI_MODEL.

decisions.statement: Rename user-visible AutoForge text to Priozar but keep legacy-describing text and exact-match integration strings unchanged
decisions.reasoning: The product name and CLI command shown to users, and the command agents are told to run, should be Priozar. Text about the legacy product, agent ids, installed hook commands, managed-block markers, package names and file or state paths are matched by existing files or other releases, so they change only with their own migrations.
consequences: Help, status, messages and generated agent, context and contract text now say Priozar and tell users to run priozar commands.
The guardrail output prefix is now Priozar guardrail; the agent-cli accepts both prefixes so a newer agent works against an older installed CLI.
Legacy migration wording, FRAMEWORK_IDENTITY.current, agent ids, the Claude hook command and the managed-block markers are unchanged and tracked by an issue.

decisions.statement: Rename the workspace packages to @cojacklabs/priozar* and let the CLI accept both package names
decisions.reasoning: FRAMEWORK_IDENTITY.successor already defines the target package names, so the rename follows it exactly, and a new test pins package.json names to it. Runtime checks that read a package name must tolerate an install from before the rename.
consequences: The root, core, protocol, sdk, providers and agent packages are now @cojacklabs/priozar, -core, -protocol, -sdk, -providers and -agent; workspace imports, dependency keys, turbo filters and the lockfile follow.
findPackageVersion accepts either CLI package name, and the Agent launcher protocol accepts an agent reporting either its new or its pre-rename package name.
Legacy-install detection, FRAMEWORK_IDENTITY.current and the legacy fixtures keep the old name. CI, deploy and changeset config are handled by a sibling task, and nothing is published.

decisions.statement: Update CI, deploy verification and changeset config to the renamed packages and keep an alias smoke test
decisions.reasoning: The workflows filter, pack and import packages by name, and the deploy workflow asserts the expected names, so leaving the old names would fail CI and release verification the moment the packages were renamed. The deprecated autoforge binary should be proven to still work during the compatibility window.
consequences: ci.yml and deploy.yml build, pack and smoke test @cojacklabs/priozar* and run priozar as the primary command, plus an autoforge version check for the alias; the changeset ignore list names the renamed agent and providers packages.
pnpm release:status still exits 1 because public packages changed without a changeset; that is a version decision tracked in the external release preparation phase, and nothing here publishes.

decisions.statement: Make priozar and priozar-agent the primary binaries, keep the autoforge names as aliases, and let the launcher fall back to an older agent
decisions.reasoning: The launcher and the CLI are released independently, so a new CLI must still find an agent installed before the rename, and existing scripts and hooks call autoforge. The deprecation notice goes only to an interactive stderr so automation and pipes see no extra output.
consequences: package.json lists priozar before autoforge, the agent package ships priozar-agent plus an autoforge-agent alias, and both aliases print a one-line notice only when stderr is a terminal.
The launcher probes priozar-agent first and falls back to autoforge-agent only when the preferred one is missing, so an incompatible new agent is never masked by an old install.
The TTY notice branch is not covered by an automated test because the tests have no pseudo-terminal; the silent non-terminal path is tested.

decisions.statement: New projects keep creating .autoforge until the Priozar release ships
decisions.reasoning: A project created as .priozar cannot be read by any already-installed autoforge CLI, including teammates, CI and the global install. Existing projects can move with migrate brand when each team is ready, so there is no need to strand anyone for new projects.
consequences: init and attach are unchanged for now; the dual-read resolver already works with either directory.
A task in the external release preparation phase flips the default to .priozar at release.

decisions.statement: Rename current docs to Priozar, rewrite naming-status passages by hand, and leave history and the registered North Star file name alone
decisions.reasoning: Current guides should describe the product users run, but regex replacement garbles text that deliberately discusses both names, and rewrote the naming workstream as if the successor were undecided. The North Star is a registered draft artifact that only an approved artifact can supersede, and approval is a human decision, so its file name stays until the maintainer approves it.
consequences: README, the current guides and the 0.26 North Star and Roadmap say Priozar and use priozar commands, package names and PRIOZAR_ guide file names; the four operational guides and the Roadmap file were renamed with their links updated and no broken relative links remain.

The transition notice and the Naming Workstream passages were rewritten to state that Priozar is selected and being implemented, without claiming that identifier reservation or legal review are complete.

Brand-transition docs, research, historical plans and the generated AUTOFORGE.md snapshot were not rewritten; the .autoforge/ state paths in docs stay accurate because new projects keep creating .autoforge until release.

decisions.statement: Rename user-visible text and commands in templates, devops, diagrams and legacy scripts but leave storage names and dev history references
decisions.reasoning: The issue and PR templates, CI templates and script output are shown to people, so they should say Priozar and tell them to run priozar. The legacy scripts also use autoforge as on-disk names such as .autoforge/runtime/autoforge.db and the legacy autoforge/ directory, and the planning workflow reads real dev/AutoForge_* files, so renaming those would orphan data or break checks.
consequences: Templates, devops CI, diagrams and script messages say Priozar and npx priozar; autoforge.config.json references stay until the root config rename task, and database, directory and dev file names are unchanged.
There were no autoforge.sh links in the repository, only the identity data, so no domain links needed changing.

decisions.statement: Teach the script readers both config file names before renaming the root file
decisions.reasoning: The root autoforge.config.json is read by the legacy scripts and the ai runtime coordinator, and the coordinator treats a missing file as passing tests, so renaming first would silently skip a project's configured tests. The scripts also only knew .autoforge and the legacy autoforge directory, so they would have failed on a migrated .priozar project.
consequences: apply_config.js and run_quality_gates.js read priozar.config.json first and fall back to autoforge.config.json, apply_config also finds a .priozar directory, and build_dist ships both names.
The coordinator and the file rename follow as separate tasks in that order; this task does not rename the file.

decisions.statement: Fix the coordinator's duplicate declaration so it can load, then dual-read priozar.config.json and .priozar
decisions.reasoning: ai/runtime/coordinator.js has had a duplicate const allowedRoots in one method since v0.4.1, so the module could not be loaded and its configured-test fallback could never run or be tested. Both declarations computed the same value, so removing the second is behavior-neutral and lets the dual-read change be proven by tests.
consequences: The coordinator now loads, resolves .priozar before .autoforge and the legacy directory, and reads priozar.config.json before autoforge.config.json for the configured test command.
A project with no config file still counts as passing, as before.
Nothing else imports the coordinator, so the previously unloadable file had no active callers.

decisions.statement: Rename the root config file to priozar.config.json now that every reader accepts both names
decisions.reasoning: The scripts and the ai runtime coordinator both read priozar.config.json first and fall back to autoforge.config.json, and tests prove it, so the root file can move without silently skipping a project's configured tests. The v0.24 legacy migration keeps reading the old name because it migrates old projects.
consequences: autoforge.config.json is now priozar.config.json, and the ai prompts, managed target files, docs, qa, change request templates and diagram name the new file.
scripts, the coordinator, build_dist and the legacy migration still mention the old name deliberately as the fallback or legacy source.
The historical expansion doc that proposes an enhanced autoforge.config.json is unchanged.

decisions.statement: CONTRIBUTING.md now names Priozar, the @cojacklabs/priozar package, bin/priozar.js and the PRIOZAR_CLI_REFERENCE link
decisions.reasoning: The CLI reference was renamed in phase 4, so the link was broken. CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md has no product name and SECURITY.md does not exist. GitHub clone URLs stay on the autoforge repo name until the human renames the repository.
consequences: Contributor docs match the current CLI. Clone URLs need updating after the repo rename in phase 6.

decisions.statement: Retired the stale AUTOFORGE.md snapshot instead of regenerating it as PRIOZAR.md
decisions.reasoning: AUTOFORGE.md was a one-off Repomix pack last touched at v0.4.1 and nothing generates or reads it; scripts/generate_snapshot.js writes REPO.md. A fresh pack is 4.9 MB against 262 KB, so committing it would bloat the repo. Git history keeps the old file.
consequences: REPO.md stays the current snapshot. The ignore lists in .prettierignore and scripts/build_dist.js now name PRIOZAR.md in case a snapshot is generated under that name later.

decisions.statement: Prettier now ignores .priozar/ and .priozar.backup-*/
decisions.reasoning: The migrated state directory is machine-written JSON; .prettierignore only covered .autoforge/, so format:check failed after the migration.
consequences: format:check passes with state under .priozar/.

decisions.statement: Applied migrate brand to this repository: state now lives in .priozar/
decisions.reasoning: Dry run listed 12 actions; the migration backed up, copied, verified and validated before removing .autoforge. doctor, recap, context and gate all pass on the local priozar CLI. The agent contract was regenerated with the priozar context command. work.json and decisions.json were gitignored by the mirrored rules but were tracked before, so I force-added them to keep them tracked.
consequences: The global autoforge 0.25.3 can no longer read this repo; use node bin/priozar.js until Priozar is installed globally. Registered projects are not migrated. Eight gitignored .autoforge.backup-* directories remain.

decisions.statement: Added docs/PRIOZAR_RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md with the human steps for the npm, GitHub and domain rename
decisions.reasoning: Publishing, repo rename and DNS are outward-facing and need credentials, so agents only prepare them. A local pack and install smoke test mirroring deploy.yml passed, the four @cojacklabs/priozar* names returned 404 on npm, and no URLs outside CONTRIBUTING.md and .changeset/README.md name the old repo.
consequences: A maintainer can run the release in order with verification and rollback steps. Nothing was published, renamed or changed in DNS.
